public_rationale: Adept's March 14 release announced $350 million in Series B financing and described an ambition to build an AI teammate trained across software tools and APIs. Its accompanying announcement contains the ambition Marcus quoted. OpenAI's contemporaneous GPT-4 documentation explicitly acknowledges hallucinations and reasoning errors. The sentence is supported as a report of funding, intended product scope, and known LLM limitations. It does not establish that Adept already had universal access or that its model had a particular error rate.
limitations: Adept's main domain blocked the page reader; the quotations come from readable reproductions on adept.futurefabric.co.
The financing figure is company-reported, with no stated audit status.
Adept described a language-directed action model, so Marcus's LLM terminology is broad.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Adept.AI just raised $350 million to let large language models access pretty much everything, despite LLMs' clear tendencies toward hallucination and unreliability.

statement.excerpt: A company called Adept.AI just raised $350 million dollars to do just that, to allow large language models to access, well, pretty much everything (aiming to “supercharge your capabilities on any software tool or API in the world” with LLMs, despite their clear tendencies towards hallucination and unreliability).

from_speaker: to allow large language models to access, well, pretty much everything
aiming to “supercharge your capabilities on any software tool or API in the world”
clear tendencies towards hallucination and unreliability
our_interpretation: Read 'just raised' as referring to the recent March 2023 financing announcement, before the March 28 post. The target period is March 1–28, 2023.
Treat the amount as the company's announced financing figure, consistent with the accompanying quotation of its stated ambition; it is not revenue, valuation, or net cash after fees.
Read 'pretty much everything' through the explicit software-tool and API qualification.
Read 'aiming' as a statement of product ambition, not a claim that universal software access had already been achieved.
Read LLM unreliability as a known tendency to produce factual or reasoning errors, not universal failure or a measured error rate for Adept's own model.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous disclosures identify a $350 million Adept financing round and an ambition to use language-directed models across software tools and APIs, while contemporary technical documentation acknowledges hallucinations and reliability limitations in LLMs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable contemporaneous records establish a materially different announced financing amount or purpose, or show that the described LLM reliability limitations were absent.

evidence.excerpt: Today, Adept announces $350M in new capital as part of its Series B financing led by General Catalyst and co-led by Spark Capital.
evidence.locator: Dated March 14, 2023 opening paragraph, second sentence
evidence.explanation: The release confirms the announced $350 million financing. It also describes the long-term goal of training an AI teammate to use every software tool and API, and says funding would support products, model training, and hiring.

evidence.excerpt: It can take complex user requests across a range of software tools and execute them, even coordinating across multiple tools when needed.
evidence.explanation: The announcement describes ACT-1's software actions and contains the broad software-tool and API ambition Marcus quoted. It presents universal reach as a goal, while describing existing functionality across a range of tools.

evidence.excerpt: Most importantly, it still is not fully reliable (it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors).
evidence.explanation: This contemporaneous disclosure supports the general reliability qualification in Marcus's sentence. It concerns GPT-4 rather than Adept's finances or an Adept-specific error rate; the same section also reports improvement over earlier models.
